summary: Revision 1 returned HUMAN_REQUIRED because Claude could not access primary sources and correctly found no repository-held mount-independent curved/straight life-line interpretation. The Director independently verified the available public-domain evidence and recorded the controlling boundary in .ai-ops/evidence/PP-RELAY-046-director-life-line-curvature.md: the only established reading is Benham's mount-bound one -- a life line running close to the thumb reduces the Mount of Venus's territory and checks its operation -- and Palmistry Path currently has no approved evidence for an independent, mount-free straight-life-line meaning. Revision 2 authors src/content/blog/beginner/curved-life-line-meaning.md, item 17 from docs/editorial-backlog.md's Next 25 list (68 -> 69 published blog posts), against that boundary rather than inventing a standalone curved-vs-straight personality axis. The article teaches comparative arc identification (wide sweep versus path close to the thumb, with no fixed angle, universal normal curve, or population cutoff), explains the verified Benham quotation already used in life-line.md -- a narrow arc 'reduces the size of the Mount of Venus, thus checking the operation of that Mount' -- and the already-published paired wide-arc/narrow-arc readings from life-line.md and mount-of-venus.md, and states directly that this site does not currently have approved evidence for a reading of the line's path detached from that mount. It does not claim no palmistry source anywhere has ever offered a separate interpretation, only that Palmistry Path's approved evidence does not currently establish one. Added one reciprocal link from life-line.md's existing 'Explore further' list; no other wording in that file's pre-existing 'Wide arc'/'Narrow arc' prose, or in mount-of-venus.md, was reopened, per the task's prohibition on rewriting the canonical pillar.
